finding_F88_THREE_OF_SEVENTEEN_SHARE_A_P.WHY_THIS_CHANGES_THE_ANALYSIS: Three of seventeen roster entries — including two tier-1 products named by the scenario itself — are one company. Every finding of the form 'N competitors do X' has been silently treating them as independent evidence. Where siblings agree, apparent market consensus may be a single portfolio decision.
findings_that_must_now_be_re_read: F-26 / F-46 refinement: 'products that hand off build decision layers; products that transact do not' — Booking.com (transacts) and Kayak (hands off) are the SAME COMPANY running both models deliberately. That strengthens the finding as a business-model claim and weakens it as a claim about independent firms converging.

F-46: Google Flights commits to all-in pricing; Kayak excludes baggage. Kayak's sibling Booking.com also says only 'includes taxes and fees'. Two of the three data points on price honesty are one company.
F-29 / F-88: 'Booking.com unlocks a discount, Google unlocks a capability' — the Booking.com half is one firm's choice, not the intermediary norm.
Any count of the form 'X of N competitors' in the final synthesis must state the sibling relationship or it overstates independence.
finding_F88_THREE_OF_SEVENTEEN_SHARE_A_P.action: Roster audit item 4. The plan's own section 2.2 argued tier composition on capability coverage and never considered corporate independence. That is a real gap in the plan, found in capture.

finding_F89_KAYAK_PUBLISHES_A_FULL_RANKI.revision_to_F75: F-75 held that the products with NO sort control explain ranking most fully, and that control and explanation are traded off. Kayak breaks that: it offers three sort tabs AND publishes the most detailed ranking document found. The trade-off framing does not survive. The corrected statement is simply that explanation VARIES enormously and is unrelated to how much control is offered.
finding_F89_KAYAK_PUBLISHES_A_FULL_RANKI.likely_cause_stated_as_inference: Inferred, not verified: this reads as EU Digital Services Act / P2B transparency compliance rather than a product choice. Both Kayak and Booking.com are EU-facing platforms. The documents' existence may be regulatory rather than voluntary — which matters, because a regulatory floor is available to Luma too and confers no differentiation.

our_product_decision_required: Decision required for the ANALYSIS: state the Booking Holdings relationship wherever a count is presented. Three of seventeen is 18% of the roster and includes two scenario-named competitors.

Decision required: if ranking transparency is a regulatory floor rather than a differentiator, Luma gains nothing by matching it. The differentiator would be explaining a ranking a traveller can ACT on — 'why is this third for me' — which no observed document does.
not_observed: the ranking document read in full — headings and samples captured only
